knee_flex.source: Leg extension guides (RitFit, e3rehab): start with the knees at about a 90-degree angle; extend the quads until the legs are nearly straight but not locked out (illustrative 5 degrees); e3rehab notes terminal knee extension creates the highest patellofemoral pressure, so stopping a few degrees short of full (0-degree) extension is the practical, joint-friendly stop

hip_flex.source: Leg extension mistake guides (ampainsoc, Art of Manliness): actively pull the hip down into the seat and keep the butt and back in contact with the pads for the whole set, a narrow band around the seated 90-degree hip angle

muscles.peakSource: RitFit / e3rehab leg extension guides: terminal knee extension is where quad effort and knee-joint load both peak, which is why form guides say to stop just short of full lockout there

mistake.name: Hips up, momentum up

tells.text: The hips lift off the seat as the weight gets heavy.
The leg bar is kicked up with a jerk and dropped back instead of a controlled extension.

mistake.source: Leg extension mistake guides (bodybuilding-wizard, ampainsoc, Art of Manliness): lifting the hips off the seat shifts tension away from the quads; bouncing or swinging the leg bar up with momentum and letting it drop removes the controlled tension the quads need

sources: Contact fact (shin pad / ankle strap): the shin pad rests at the ankles, feet facing forward (RitFit); a real-world description, not a numeric `machine.settings` value this research can cite
